It speaks straight to the viewer and gives away the punchline idea within 7 words. (b) It sticks to one topic, and the surprising image is the source's: mother cats bring prey to kittens to teach them to hunt, so your cat may think you will starve. (c) It is tight at 78 words, 11 lines and about 27 seconds, and it ends on the strongest line in the source, "This poor thing is going to starve without me." (d) It has the cleanest loop: "So that mouse may be a lesson, because / Your cat may think you can't hunt." reads as one sentence. (e) It keeps all three of the source's hedges ("Nobody knows for sure", "one popular theory", "may").

Candidate 2: the "Zero" hook does not mention cats or mice in its first second. A stone tablet in a living room is a strange image, and the script drops the quote that makes the payoff. Candidate 3: it brings in a "gift" framing the source never uses. It also states "It's a lesson, not a present." with no hedge, which breaks the hedging rule.

Fixes made to Candidate 1 (narration unchanged, all edits are in scenes):
1. Removed the "HUNTING LESSON" text from the chalkboard. The renderer only writes quoted numbers on stone tablets, so free text is risky.
2. Replaced "kittens" with small {CAT} tokens, because kittens are not a supported character.
3. Dropped "den", which is not a supported setting, and kept desert.
4. Replaced "chips" and "crumbs", which are not supported props, with a lazy pose on the couch.
5. Changed "pot" to the supported "clay jar".
6. Mapped unsupported emotions to the supported ones: disappointed to smug, proud to happy, panic to shocked, pitying to sad.
7. Added a setting keyword ("in the living room") to the one scene that had none.
8. Kept every scene to 1-3 characters.

final.yt_description: Every night, chimpanzees build a brand new bed high in the trees. Scientists found their nests had far fewer bacteria than human beds. Full story: tap the video link on this Short. #shorts #chimpanzee #sleep
